# LearnFlex — Machine-Readable Platform Description

Canonical URL: https://learnflex.onrender.com/
Project name: LearnFlex
Target curriculum: CBSE (Central Board of Secondary Education, India), Classes 6–10, with NCERT textbook chapter catalogues where represented

## Platform summary
LearnFlex is a demonstration adaptive-learning and formative-practice platform for CBSE Classes 6–10. It uses deterministic, explainable rules to select practice tiers from recent correctness and learner-reported confidence. It does not depend on an external generative-AI API.

## Curriculum catalogue
- 528 chapter and curricular activity modules are included in the current generated catalogue.
- Subjects include Mathematics, Science, Social Studies, English, Hindi, Sanskrit, Arts Education, Physical Education and Well-being, Vocational Education, and the Class 9 Individuals in Society modules.
- Arts, PE, Vocational and other explicitly identified curricular modules are activities, not necessarily textbook chapters.
- The catalogue maps chapter titles and includes original generated lesson summaries and practice drafts. These are not official NCERT questions and require subject-teacher review.
- Class/subject offerings and textbook editions must be checked against each school's prescribed course.

## Core Pedagogical & Adaptive Architecture

### Four-Tier Difficulty Framework
- Foundation: foundational review and easier concept checks.
- Reinforcement: guided practice for correct-but-uncertain responses and repeated errors.
- Standard: grade-level practice drafts.
- Challenge: higher-order application drafts.

## Adaptive learning
- Four practice tiers are represented: Foundation, Reinforcement, Standard and Challenge.
- Selection uses correctness and self-reported confidence. The primary assessment can append further questions based on recent responses.
- Option feedback is available for mapped answer choices. It is a prompt for discussion, not a clinical or definitive diagnosis.
- Explicit prerequisite links are supplied for a limited set of selected Mathematics and Science concept sequences. This is not a complete prerequisite graph for all modules.

## Offline support
- The application shell and selected lesson/question packs can be cached for offline access after download.
- Learning changes can be saved locally and queued for later synchronization when a valid authenticated server session is available.
- Full offline behavior depends on prior download, browser storage, and service-worker support. Not every server function is available offline.

## Privacy and security safeguards
- Public registration is restricted to student accounts; teacher accounts must be provisioned by an authorized operator.
- Teacher access is scoped by class, school and section on the backend.
- Passwords are hashed on the server; browser storage does not retain plaintext passwords. Session bearer tokens are kept in session storage.
- This demonstration is not a legal certification of compliance with the DPDP Act or any other privacy law. A school/legal/security review is required before real student data is used.
- Do not enter real student data in the public demonstration.

## Runtime and architecture
- Backend: Node.js 22.5+ with built-in HTTP server and `node:sqlite`; atomic JSON fallback is available.
- Frontend: vanilla JavaScript, CSS and HTML.
- Offline persistence: IndexedDB packs and an outbox; the app also keeps a compact local progress snapshot.
- Tests cover syntax, backend API contracts, adaptive routing contracts and source-level offline contracts. Browser-based end-to-end testing requires a compatible browser runtime and must be reported separately.

## Limitations
- Generated practice questions and lesson summaries require educator validation.
- Prerequisite coverage is partial.
- Offline behavior should be verified in the target browser/device before claiming full offline operation.
- SEO metadata and machine-readable descriptions do not guarantee search ranking or AI-search inclusion.
